title: How to hear this sermon
english: This is a listening version of John Wesley's sermon, The Great Privilege of Those That Are Born of God. It is the sermon as printed in John Wesley's 1771 Works. Rendered in modern English.

title: Whoever is born of God
english: Whoever is born of God does not commit sin (1 John 3:9). 1 John 3:9.

title: Justification and the new birth
english: It has often been supposed that being born of God was the same thing as being justified, and that the new birth and justification were only different expressions for the same thing. It is certain, on the one hand, that whoever is justified is also born of God, and on the other, that whoever is born of God is also justified. Yes, both these gifts of God are given to every believer in one and the same moment. In one point of time his sins are blotted out (Acts 3:19), and he is born again of God.

title: A relative change, and a real one
english: But though it is allowed that justification and the new birth are, in point of time, inseparable from each other, they are easily distinguished. They are not the same. They are things of a widely different nature. Justification implies only a relative change. The new birth is a real change. God, in justifying us, does something for us. In begetting us again, he does the work in us. The former changes our outward relation to God, so that of enemies we become children. By the latter our inmost souls are changed, so that of sinners we become saints. The one restores us to the favor of God. The other restores us to the image of God. The one is the taking away of the guilt. The other is the taking away of the power of sin. So although they are joined together in point of time, they are of wholly distinct natures.

title: Where the confusion began
english: Not discerning this, not observing the wide difference between being justified and being born again, has caused very great confusion of thought in many who have written on this subject. Particularly when they have attempted to explain this great privilege of the children of God, and to show how whoever is born of God does not commit sin.

title: The two questions
english: In order to grasp this clearly, it may be necessary, first, to consider the proper meaning of that expression, "Whoever is born of God," and second, to inquire in what sense he does not commit sin.

title: Not barely being baptized
english: First, we are to consider the proper meaning of that expression, "Whoever is born of God." In general, from all the passages of holy scripture in which this expression, being born of God, occurs, we may learn that it implies not barely being baptized, or any outward change whatever. It is a vast inward change, a change wrought in the soul by the operation of the Holy Ghost. A change in the whole manner of our existence. For from the moment we are born of God, we live in quite another manner than we did before. We are, as it were, in another world.

title: The figure of a birth
english: The ground and reason of the expression is easy to understand. When we undergo this great change, we may with much propriety be said to be born again, because there is so near a resemblance between the circumstances of the natural birth and of the spiritual birth. To consider the circumstances of the natural birth is the easiest way to understand the spiritual.

title: Before the child is born
english: The child who is not yet born does indeed subsist by the air, as does everything which has life. But he does not feel it, nor anything else, except in a very dull and imperfect manner. He hears little, if at all, the organs of hearing being as yet closed up. He sees nothing, his eyes fast shut, and he is surrounded with utter darkness. There are, it may be, some faint beginnings of life when the time of his birth draws near, and some motion that follows, by which he is distinguished from a mere mass of matter. But he has no senses. All these avenues of the soul are still quite shut up. Consequently he has scarce any intercourse with this visible world, nor any knowledge, conception, or idea of the things that occur in it.

title: The world is very near
english: The reason he who is not yet born is wholly a stranger to the visible world is not that the world is far off. It is very near. It surrounds him on every side. But partly he has not those senses. They are not yet opened in his soul, and by them alone it is possible to have commerce with the material world. And partly so thick a veil is cast between that he can discern nothing through it.

title: When the child is born
english: But no sooner is the child born into the world than he exists in quite a different manner. He now feels the air with which he is surrounded, and which pours into him from every side, as fast as he alternately breathes it back, to sustain the flame of life. And from this springs a continual increase of strength, of motion, and of sensation, all the bodily senses being now awakened and furnished with their proper objects.

title: Eyes and ears
english: His eyes are now opened to perceive the light, which, silently flowing in upon them, discloses not only itself but an infinite variety of things with which before he was wholly unacquainted. His ears are unclosed, and sounds rush in with endless diversity. Every sense is employed upon such objects as are peculiarly suitable to it. And by these inlets the soul, having an open intercourse with the visible world, acquires more and more knowledge of sensible things, of all the things which are under the sun.

title: Before a person is born of God
english: So it is with the person who is born of God. Before that great change is wrought, although he subsists by him in whom all who have life live, and move, and have their being (Acts 17:28), yet he is not sensible of God. He does not feel. He has no inward consciousness of his presence. He does not perceive that divine breath of life, without which he cannot subsist a moment. Nor is he sensible of any of the things of God. They make no impression upon his soul. God is continually calling to him from on high, but he does not hear. His ears are shut, so that the voice of the charmer (Psalm 58:5) is lost to him, however wisely he charms. He does not see the things of the Spirit of God (1 Corinthians 2:14), the eyes of his understanding (Ephesians 1:18) being closed, and utter darkness covering his whole soul, surrounding him on every side. It is true he may have some faint dawnings of life, some small beginnings of spiritual motion. But as yet he has no spiritual senses capable of discerning spiritual objects. Consequently he does not discern the things of the Spirit of God (1 Corinthians 2:14). He cannot know them, because they are spiritually discerned (1 Corinthians 2:14).

title: In the midst of the invisible world
english: Hence he has scarce any knowledge of the invisible world, as he has scarce any intercourse with it. Not that it is far off. No. He is in the midst of it. It encompasses him round about. The other world, as we usually call it, is not far from every one of us (Acts 17:27). It is above, and beneath, and on every side. Only the natural man does not discern it (1 Corinthians 2:14). Partly because he has no spiritual senses, by which alone we can discern the things of God. Partly because so thick a veil is interposed that he does not know how to penetrate it.

title: The breath of God
english: But when he is born of God, born of the Spirit, how is the manner of his existence changed? His whole soul is now sensible of God, and he can say by sure experience, "You are about my bed, and about my path (Psalm 139:3). I feel you in all my ways. You beset me behind and before, and lay your hand upon me" (Psalm 139:5). The Spirit, or breath, of God is immediately inspired, breathed into the newborn soul. And the same breath which comes from God returns to God. As it is continually received by faith, so it is continually rendered back by love, by prayer, and praise, and thanksgiving. Love, and praise, and prayer are the breath of every soul which is truly born of God. And by this new kind of spiritual respiration, spiritual life is not only sustained but increased day by day, together with spiritual strength, and motion, and sensation, all the senses of the soul being now awake and capable of discerning spiritual good and evil.

title: He sees him who is invisible
english: The eyes of his understanding are now open, and he sees him who is invisible (Hebrews 11:27). He sees the exceeding greatness of his power (Ephesians 1:19), and of his love toward those who believe. He sees that God is merciful to him, a sinner, and that he is reconciled through the Son of his love (Colossians 1:13). He clearly perceives both the pardoning love of God and all his exceeding great and precious promises (2 Peter 1:4). God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, has shone, and does shine, in his heart, to enlighten him with the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ (2 Corinthians 4:6). All the darkness is now passed, and he abides in the light of God's countenance.

title: He knows the voice of his Shepherd
english: His ears are now opened, and the voice of God no longer calls in vain. He hears and obeys the heavenly calling. He knows the voice of his Shepherd (John 10:4). All his spiritual senses being now awakened, he has a clear intercourse with the invisible world. And hence he knows more and more of the things which before it could not enter into his heart to conceive (1 Corinthians 2:9). He now knows what the peace of God is, what joy in the Holy Ghost (Romans 14:17) is, what the love of God is which is shed abroad (Romans 5:5) in the hearts of those who believe in him through Christ Jesus. Thus the veil is removed which before intercepted the light and voice, the knowledge and love of God. He who is born of the Spirit dwells in love, dwells in God, and God in him (1 John 4:16).

title: He does not commit sin
english: Having considered the meaning of that expression, "whoever is born of God," it remains, in the second place, to inquire in what sense he does not commit sin.

title: While he keeps himself
english: Now one who is so born of God, as has been described above, continually receives into his soul the breath of life from God, the gracious influence of his Spirit, and continually renders it back. He believes and loves. By faith he perceives the continual actings of God upon his spirit, and by a kind of spiritual reaction he returns the grace he receives, in unceasing love, and praise, and prayer. Such a one not only does not commit sin while he thus keeps himself. So long as this seed remains in him, he cannot sin, because he is born of God (1 John 3:9).

title: Outward sin
english: By sin I here understand outward sin, according to the plain, common meaning of the word. An actual, voluntary transgression of the law, of the revealed, written law of God, of any commandment of God acknowledged to be such at the time it is transgressed. But whoever is born of God, while he abides in faith and love, and in the spirit of prayer and thanksgiving, not only does not, but cannot, commit sin in this way.

So long as he thus believes in God through Christ, and loves him, and is pouring out his heart before him, he cannot voluntarily transgress any command of God, either by speaking or by acting what he knows God has forbidden. So long as that seed remains in him, that loving, praying, thankful faith compels him to refrain from whatever he knows to be an abomination in the sight of God (Luke 16:15).

title: The difficulty
english: But here a difficulty will immediately occur, one that to many has appeared insuperable, and has induced them to deny the plain assertion of the apostle, and to give up the privilege of the children of God.

title: They did commit sin
english: It is plain, in fact, that those whom we cannot deny to have been truly born of God, the Spirit of God having given us in his word this infallible testimony concerning them, nevertheless not only could, but did, commit sin, even gross, outward sin. They did transgress the plain, known laws of God, speaking or acting what they knew he had forbidden.

title: David
english: Thus David was unquestionably born of God before he was anointed king over Israel. He knew in whom he had believed (2 Timothy 1:12). He was strong in faith, giving glory to God (Romans 4:20). "The Lord," he says, "is my shepherd, therefore I can lack nothing (Psalm 23:1). He shall feed me in green pastures, and lead me forth beside the waters of comfort (Psalm 23:2). Yes, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death (Psalm 23:4), I will fear no evil, for you are with me."

He was filled with love, such as often constrained him to cry out, "I will love you, O Lord, my God. The Lord is my stony rock and my defense, the horn also of my salvation, and my refuge" (Psalm 18:2). He was a man of prayer, pouring out his soul before God in all circumstances of life, and abundant in praises and thanksgiving. "Your praise," he says, "shall ever be in my mouth (Psalm 34:1). You are my God, and I will thank you (Psalm 118:28). You are my God, and I will praise you" (Psalm 118:28). And yet such a child of God could, and did, commit sin. Yes, the horrid sins of adultery and murder.

title: Barnabas
english: And even after the Holy Ghost was more largely given, after life and immortality were brought to light by the gospel (2 Timothy 1:10), we do not lack instances of the same melancholy kind, which were also doubtless written for our instruction (1 Corinthians 10:11).

Thus the man who, probably from his selling all that he had and bringing the price for the relief of his poor brothers, was surnamed Barnabas by the apostles themselves, that is, the son of consolation (Acts 4:36). He was so honored at Antioch as to be selected with Saul, out of all the disciples, to carry their relief to the brothers in Judea. This Barnabas, who at his return from Judea was, by the peculiar direction of the Holy Ghost, solemnly separated from the other prophets and teachers for the work to which God had called him, even to accompany the great apostle among the Gentiles and to be his fellow laborer in every place.

Nevertheless he was afterward so sharp in his contention with Saint Paul, because he thought it not good to take with them John, in his visiting the brothers a second time, John who had departed from them from Pamphylia (Acts 15:38) and did not go with them to the work, that he himself also departed from the work. He took John and sailed to Cyprus (Acts 15:39), forsaking the one to whom he had been joined in so immediate a manner by the Holy Ghost.

title: Peter at Antioch
english: An instance more astonishing than both of these is given by Saint Paul in his letter to the Galatians. When Peter, the zealous, the first of the apostles, one of the three most highly favored by his Lord, had come to Antioch, "I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed" (Galatians 2:11). For before certain men came from James, he ate with the Gentiles, the heathens converted to the Christian faith, as one who had been peculiarly taught by God that he should not call any man common or unclean (Acts 10:28). But when they had come, he separated himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision. And the other Jews pretended likewise with him, so much that Barnabas also was carried away with their pretense.

But when I saw that they did not walk uprightly, according to the truth of the gospel (Galatians 2:14), I said to Peter before them all, "If you, being a Jew, live after the manner of the Gentiles, not regarding the ceremonial law of Moses, why do you compel the Gentiles to live as the Jews do?" Here too is plain, undeniable sin, committed by one who was undoubtedly born of God. But how can this be reconciled with the assertion of Saint John, if taken in the obvious literal meaning, that whoever is born of God does not commit sin?

title: If he does not keep himself
english: I answer, what has long been observed is this. So long as he who is born of God keeps himself, which he is able to do by the grace of God, the wicked one does not touch him (1 John 5:18). But if he does not keep himself, if he does not abide in the faith, he may commit sin even as another man.

title: He fell, step by step
english: It is easy, therefore, to understand how any of these children of God might be moved from his own steadfastness, and yet the great truth of God, declared by the apostle, remain steadfast and unshaken. He did not keep himself by that grace of God which was sufficient for him. He fell, step by step. First into negative, inward sin, not stirring up the gift of God which was in him (2 Timothy 1:6), not watching toward prayer (1 Peter 4:7), not pressing on to the mark of the prize of his high calling (Philippians 3:14). Then into positive inward sin, inclining to wickedness with his heart, giving way to some evil desire or temper. Next he lost his faith, his sight of a pardoning God, and consequently his love of God. And being then weak, and like another man, he was capable of committing even outward sin.

title: Whom have I in heaven but you
english: To explain this by a particular instance. David was born of God, and saw God by faith. He loved God in sincerity. He could truly say, "Whom have I in heaven but you (Psalm 73:25)? And there is none upon earth, neither person nor thing, that I desire in comparison of you." But still there remained in his heart that corruption of nature which is the seed of all evil.

title: Bathsheba
english: He was walking upon the roof of his house, probably praising the God whom his soul loved, when he looked down and saw Bathsheba. He felt a temptation, a thought which tended to evil. The Spirit of God did not fail to convince him of this. He doubtless heard and knew the warning voice. But he yielded in some measure to the thought, and the temptation began to prevail over him. By this his spirit was sullied. He saw God still, but it was more dimly than before. He loved God still, but not in the same degree, not with the same strength and ardor of affection. Yet God checked him again, though his Spirit was grieved, and his voice, though fainter and fainter, still whispered, "Sin lies at the door (Genesis 4:7). Look to me, and be saved" (Isaiah 45:22). But he would not hear. He looked again, not to God, but to the forbidden object, until nature was superior to grace, and kindled lust in his soul.

title: He rushed on
english: The eye of his mind was now closed again, and God vanished out of his sight. Faith, the divine, supernatural intercourse with God, and the love of God, ceased together. He then rushed on, as a horse into the battle (Jeremiah 8:6), and knowingly committed the outward sin.

title: Eight steps
english: You see the unquestionable progress from grace to sin. Thus it goes on, from step to step. First, the divine seed of loving, conquering faith remains in him who is born of God. He keeps himself, by the grace of God, and cannot commit sin. Second, a temptation arises, whether from the world, the flesh, or the devil. It matters not. Third, the Spirit of God gives him warning that sin is near, and bids him more abundantly watch toward prayer. Fourth, he gives way, in some degree, to the temptation, which now begins to grow pleasing to him. Fifth, the Holy Spirit is grieved. His faith is weakened, and his love of God grows cold. Sixth, the Spirit reproves him more sharply, and says, "This is the way (Isaiah 30:21). Walk in it" (Isaiah 30:21). Seventh, he turns away from the painful voice of God, and listens to the pleasing voice of the tempter. Eighth, evil desire begins and spreads in his soul, until faith and love vanish away. He is then capable of committing outward sin, the power of the Lord being departed from him (Judges 16:20).

title: Peter kept himself
english: To explain this by another instance. The apostle Peter was full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and by this, keeping himself, he had a conscience void of offense toward God and toward man (Acts 24:16).

title: What God had cleansed
english: Walking thus in simplicity and godly sincerity, before those certain men came from James, he ate with the Gentiles, knowing that what God had cleansed was not common or unclean (Acts 10:28) (Acts 10:15).

title: The praise of men
english: But when they had come, a temptation arose in his heart to fear those of the circumcision, the Jewish converts who were zealous for circumcision and the other rites of the Mosaic law, and to regard the favor and praise of these men more than the praise of God (John 12:43).

title: Sinful fear of man
english: He was warned by the Spirit that sin was near. Nevertheless he yielded to it in some degree, even to a sinful fear of man, and his faith and love were proportionally weakened.

title: He quenched the Spirit
english: God reproved him again for giving place to the devil (Ephesians 4:27). Yet he would not listen to the voice of his Shepherd (John 10:4), but gave himself up to that slavish fear, and thereby quenched the Spirit (1 Thessalonians 5:19).

title: The outward sin
english: Then God disappeared, and, faith and love being extinct, he committed the outward sin. Not walking uprightly, not according to the truth of the gospel, he separated himself from his Christian brothers, and by his evil example, if not by advice also, compelled even the Gentiles to live after the manner of the Jews, to entangle themselves again with that yoke of bondage (Galatians 5:1) from which Christ had set them free.

title: He may commit all manner of sin
english: Thus it is unquestionably true that he who is born of God, keeping himself, does not, and cannot, commit sin. And yet, if he does not keep himself, he may commit all manner of sin with greediness (Ephesians 4:19).

title: Does sin come before the loss of faith
english: From the preceding considerations we may learn, first, to give a clear and incontestable answer to a question which has frequently perplexed many who were sincere of heart. Does sin precede or follow the loss of faith? Does a child of God first commit sin, and thereby lose his faith? Or does he lose his faith first, before he can commit sin?

title: Inward sin first
english: I answer, some sin of omission, at least, must necessarily precede the loss of faith. Some inward sin. But the loss of faith must precede the committing of outward sin.

title: Drawn out by our own desire
english: The more any believer examines his own heart, the more he will be convinced of this. Faith working by love excludes both inward and outward sin from a soul watching toward prayer (1 Peter 4:7). Nevertheless we are, even then, liable to temptation, particularly to the sin that so easily beset us (Hebrews 12:1). If the loving eye of the soul is steadily fixed on God, the temptation soon vanishes. But if not, if we are drawn out of God by our own desire (James 1:14), as the apostle James speaks, and caught by the bait of present or promised pleasure, then that desire, conceived in us, brings forth sin (James 1:15). And having, by that inward sin, destroyed our faith, it casts us headlong into the snare of the devil (2 Timothy 2:26), so that we may commit any outward sin whatever.

title: Breathing back what God breathes in
english: From what has been said we may learn, second, what the life of God in the soul of a believer is, what it properly consists in, and what is immediately and necessarily implied in it. It immediately and necessarily implies the continual inspiration of God's Holy Spirit. God breathing into the soul, and the soul breathing back what it first receives from God. A continual action of God upon the soul, and a reaction of the soul upon God. An unceasing presence of God, the loving, pardoning God, manifested to the heart and perceived by faith. And an unceasing return of love, praise, and prayer, offering up all the thoughts of our hearts, all the words of our tongues, all the works of our hands, all our body, soul, and spirit, to be a holy sacrifice, acceptable to God in Christ Jesus (Romans 12:1).

title: If the soul does not answer
english: And hence we may, third, infer the absolute necessity of this reaction of the soul, whatever it is called, in order to the continuance of the divine life in it. For it plainly appears that God does not continue to act upon the soul unless the soul reacts upon God. He goes before us, indeed, with the blessings of his goodness (Psalm 21:3). He first loves us, and manifests himself to us. While we are yet far off (Luke 15:20), he calls us to himself and shines upon our hearts. But if we do not then love him who first loved us (1 John 4:19), if we will not listen to his voice, if we turn our eye away from him and will not attend to the light which he pours upon us, his Spirit will not always strive (Genesis 6:3). He will gradually withdraw, and leave us to the darkness of our own hearts. He will not continue to breathe into our soul unless our soul breathes toward him again, unless our love, and prayer, and thanksgiving return to him, a sacrifice with which he is well pleased.

title: Be not high-minded, but fear
english: Let us learn, last, to follow that direction of the great apostle: "Be not high-minded, but fear" (Romans 11:20). Let us fear sin more than death or hell. Let us have a jealous fear, though not a painful one, lest we should lean on our own deceitful hearts. "Let him who stands take heed, lest he fall" (1 Corinthians 10:12). Even he who now stands fast in the grace of God, in the faith that overcomes the world (1 John 5:4), may nevertheless fall into inward sin, and thereby make shipwreck of his faith (1 Timothy 1:19). And how easily, then, will outward sin regain its dominion over him?

You, therefore, man of God, watch always, that you may always hear the voice of God. Watch, that you may pray without ceasing (1 Thessalonians 5:17), at all times and in all places, pouring out your heart before him. So shall you always believe, and always love, and never commit sin.
